subject: SOC 2 packet — any blockers on review?
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Graves <tom.graves@fintechco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood + FintechCo discovery recap

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery:  

- Primary goals: reduce inference cost on embeddings-heavy workflows and get stable sub-200ms latency for customer-facing chat.
- Current blockers: security review + procurement timeline, and clarifying data retention/KV cache behavior for PII.
- Next steps we agreed: I’ll send over our SOC 2 packet and scope doc for security review; David (cc’d) can join a technical security call next week if helpful; procurement (Aisha) will want the pricing/term sheet once security is satisfied.

Deliverables I’ll share today: SOC 2 packet + scope spreadsheet + a short summary of our deployment options (hosted vs. dedicated).  

Would you be able to confirm who on your security/procurement teams should receive the packet so we don’t miss anyone? Also flag any specific questions we should surface for the security call.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Tom Graves <tom.graves@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 17:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood + FintechCo discovery recap

Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the recap.

Please send the SOC 2 packet and scope to me and Aisha (cc’d). I’ll loop in our security engineer if there are technical questions, but initial reviewers will be me and Aisha. Two quick asks up front:

1) Can you include a one-page summary of what data you persist (if any) and retention defaults?
2) Also include the specific audit period for the attached SOC 2 (dates).

If you can get the packet today that would be great — then we can try to book a 30m security sync next week.

Tom Graves
Head of Security | FintechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Graves <tom.graves@fintechco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:08:20 -0700
Subject: Redwood SOC 2 packet + scope (per request)

Tom / Aisha —

Attaching our SOC 2 packet and a short scope spreadsheet. Highlights included in the packet:
- SOC 2 Type II report for period 2025-08-01 through 2026-01-31
- Summary of data processing and default retention policies (see page 3) — we do not persist customer prompt text by default; KV cache used for session context is configurable and can be disabled.
- Encryption and key management summary (KMS/HSM options) and audit logging references.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Packet_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 2.3MB); redwood-soc2-scope.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

David — if you’re available, would love you to join a short security sync next week to answer any technical questions around KV cache and retentions.

Tom/Aisha — can you confirm preferred time windows for a 30m call next week?

Thanks —
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Just bumping this up the thread — wanted to check if anything in the SOC 2 packet or scope spreadsheet looks like a blocker for moving forward. If priorities/timing have changed on your side, totally fine — just want to understand where this sits so we can coordinate the procurement timeline.

We still have a couple of 30m slots open next week for the security sync (David will be on the call). If it helps, I can propose times based on your timezone.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Quick follow — SOC 2 packet review and next steps

Hi Marissa — apologies for the delay, I was out of office last week. Thanks for the packet, that answers most items. Two quick items our security reviewer flagged that would be helpful to cover on the sync:

1) Data retention defaults for KV cache — we need to confirm whether session KV can be set to 0 retention and what impact that has on latency/cost.
2) Audit log retention and whether logs containing request metadata can be exported to our S3 for long-term retention (we may have separate policies for longer-term retention).

Can we book 30m on Tue 2026-05-12 between 09:00–12:00 PT? David (cc’d) — if you can join and speak to KV/cache behavior that would be ideal. Aisha, I’ll coordinate procurement timelines after the security call.

Thanks —
Tom
Head of Security | FintechCo
